Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 01:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo invite time mismatch — likely floating TZ in ICS

Hey Soojin —

This is a classic case of a forwarded ICS losing the TZID anchor and being interpreted as a "floating" time by recipients' calendar clients. When that happens:
- Google Calendar will try to map the time to the recipient's default timezone if the event lacks an explicit TZID in DTSTART/DTEND.
- Forwarding through some mail clients strips the VTIMEZONE block or replaces it with a UTC timestamp, which can make the event show up shifted.

Short fixes we can do:
1) Re-issue a new invite from the Redwood calendar (not forwarded) that includes an explicit VTIMEZONE and local TZID (e.g., America/Los_Angeles).
2) Attach a small note in the invite description with the canonical times in major regions so recipients see the cross-region mapping: 09:00 PDT / 12:00 EDT / 16:00 BST / 02:00 AEST (next day).
3) If a recipient already has a bad instance, ask them to delete the old invite before accepting the new one.

I'll draft a corrected invite body you can paste into the event description. Also add corrected-invite.ics as a fresh attachment from the Redwood calendar — that usually resolves it.

Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
